question: Build a peer comp table for four analog and mixed-signal semiconductor companies: Texas Instruments, Analog Devices, Microchip Technology and NXP Semiconductors. Alignment rule: for each company use its own fiscal quarter that ended between April 1, 2026 and July 31, 2026 (inclusive); do not calendarize or move any company to a different quarter. Each company has exactly one such quarter. For that quarter report, using GAAP figures from the company's SEC filings as of October 3, 2026: (1) revenue in USD millions; (2) year-over-year revenue growth in % versus the same fiscal quarter a year earlier; (3) gross margin in % = gross profit / revenue; (4) operating margin in % = GAAP operating income / revenue. Also state the fiscal quarter label and quarter-end date used for each company.
company: Texas Instruments (TXN; FY ends Dec 31); Analog Devices (ADI; FY ends Saturday closest to Oct 31); Microchip Technology (MCHP; FY ends Mar 31); NXP Semiconductors (NXPI; FY ends Dec 31)
failure_mode: Calendarizing or using a common quarter instead of each company's own fiscal quarter in the window (e.g., ADI's fiscal Q3 ended Aug 1, 2026, one day outside the window, and TXN/MCHP quarters ended Mar 31, 2026 are also outside it); using non-GAAP/adjusted margins from press releases; computing growth sequentially instead of year over year; thousands-vs-millions scaling errors (ADI reports in thousands); misreading ADI's 'Gross margin' line or Microchip's 'Net sales' line.
expected_source: Form 10-Q filings for each company's in-window quarter (TXN filed 2026-07-24; ADI filed 2026-05-20; MCHP filed 2026-08-06; NXP filed 2026-07-28), cross-checked to each company's 8-K Exhibit 99.1 earnings release; EDGAR submissions index to confirm the latest quarter. XBRL companyfacts for TXN, ADI, MCHP (NXP's 2026-07-28 10-Q was not yet in companyfacts, so NXP is verified from the filing text and release).
grading: Graded cell by cell: each value within tolerance and for the stated period; a missing cell counts as wrong.
why_analysts_ask: Peer comps across companies with different fiscal calendars are a daily analyst pull; the alignment rule and GAAP margin definitions are where comps tables usually go wrong.

question: Build a trailing-twelve-month (TTM) comp table for four U.S. restaurant companies: Darden Restaurants, Brinker International, Cracker Barrel Old Country Store and The Cheesecake Factory. Define TTM as the last four reported fiscal quarters, i.e. latest fiscal year + current fiscal year-to-date - prior-year year-to-date (when the most recent reported quarter is the fiscal fourth quarter, TTM equals that fiscal year); do not adjust for 52/53-week differences. State the TTM end date used for each company.

expected_source: Darden: FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 2026-07-24) and Q1 FY2027 Form 10-Q (filed 2026-10-02; prior-year quarter comparatives in the same 10-Q); Brinker: FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 2026-08-19); Cracker Barrel: FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 2026-09-25); Cheesecake Factory: FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-23) and Q2 2026 Form 10-Q (filed 2026-08-03). question: Build a balance-sheet comp table for four U.S. retailers: TJX Companies, Ross Stores, Lowe's and Tractor Supply. Use each company's latest reported balance sheet as of October 3, 2026 (the most recent 10-Q or 10-K) and state its balance-sheet date. Report, in USD millions: (1) cash and cash equivalents (exclude short-term investments and restricted cash); (2) total debt = current portion of long-term debt + long-term debt (non-current portion), as presented on the face of the balance sheet, excluding operating lease liabilities, separately presented finance lease liabilities and any commercial paper or short-term borrowings; (3) net debt = total debt - cash and cash equivalents (a negative number means net cash).

failure_mode: Using the fiscal year-end balance sheet (Jan 30-31, 2026 / Dec 27, 2025) instead of the latest quarter (Aug 1, Jul 31 or Jun 27, 2026); including operating or finance lease liabilities in debt; omitting the current portion of long-term debt (TJX 1,000; Ross 241.5; Lowe's 2,352); sign error on net debt (TJX and Ross are in net cash); scaling errors (Ross and Tractor Supply report in thousands); assuming Tractor Supply has a current portion of long-term debt (its balance sheet shows none).

why_analysts_ask: Leverage and net-debt comps feed EV bridges and credit screens; analysts must pull the latest quarter-end balance sheet and apply one consistent debt definition across peers.

question: For The Estee Lauder Companies (fiscal year ends June 30), report GAAP gross margin (gross profit / net sales, in %) and GAAP operating margin (operating income (loss) / net sales, in %) for each of its last four reported fiscal quarters as of October 3, 2026. Label each quarter with its fiscal quarter, fiscal year and period-end date. Use GAAP figures as reported (not adjusted/non-GAAP); fourth-quarter results are not separately filed on a 10-Q.
company: The Estee Lauder Companies Inc. (EL; FY ends June 30)
failure_mode: Taking fiscal Q3 (Mar 31, 2026) as the latest quarter because the 10-K arrived on Aug 19, 2026; not deriving Q4 FY2026 as FY2026 minus nine months (net sales 3,627; gross profit 2,737; operating loss of 39, i.e. a -1.08% operating margin); using adjusted operating income (Q4 adjusted 267, about 7.4%) instead of GAAP; dropping the negative sign on the Q4 operating margin; labeling quarters with the wrong fiscal year.
expected_source: Estee Lauder Forms 10-Q for Q1 FY2026 (filed 2025-10-30), Q2 FY2026 (filed 2026-02-05) and Q3 FY2026 (filed 2026-05-01); Form 10-K FY2026 (filed 2026-08-19) minus nine months in the Q3 10-Q for Q4 FY2026; matched to the Q4 FY2026 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (filed 2026-08-19). EDGAR submissions index confirms no later quarter reported by 2026-10-03.
grading: Graded cell by cell: each value within tolerance and for the stated period; a missing cell counts as wrong.
why_analysts_ask: Margin trends by quarter are a core diagnostic for turnaround stories; the derived fourth quarter, with restructuring charges driving a GAAP operating loss, is exactly where GAAP and adjusted views diverge.
